es: Identificar el titular, la petición y el plazo de un mensaje y separar lo esencial del detalle de apoyo, incluso cuando el contexto llega antes.

teaching.en: Lead with the headline and say what you need straight away: we need three more volunteers for Saturday morning, and the list closes on Thursday.
teaching.es: Empieza por el titular y di enseguida lo que necesitas: hacen falta tres voluntarios más para el sábado por la mañana y la lista se cierra el jueves.
teaching.explanationEs: Lead with + nombre: pones primero lo que el lector necesita. El titular dice qué pasa o qué se pide.
segments: Lead with the headline and say what you need straight away: we need
three more volunteers for Saturday morning, and the list closes on Thursday.
teaching.audioText: Lead with the headline and say what you need straight away: we need three more volunteers for Saturday morning, and the list closes on Thursday.

teaching.en: My request is simple: confirm by Thursday noon whether you can cover a shift, because the caterer needs a final number before she places the order.
teaching.es: Mi petición es sencilla: confirma antes del jueves a mediodía si puedes cubrir un turno, porque la empresa de catering necesita un número definitivo antes de hacer el pedido.
teaching.explanationEs: Cover a shift es la colocación habitual para ocupar el turno de otra persona; by + día marca el plazo.
segments: My request is simple: confirm by Thursday noon whether you can cover a
shift, because the caterer needs a final number before she places the order.
teaching.audioText: My request is simple: confirm by Thursday noon whether you can cover a shift, because the caterer needs a final number before she places the order.

teaching.en: Some background can help, but it should follow the request: last year only twelve people came, so we moved the event to a weekend.
teaching.es: Algo de contexto puede ayudar, pero debe ir después de la petición: el año pasado solo vinieron doce personas, así que movimos el evento a un fin de semana.
teaching.explanationEs: El background explica el porqué. Va después de lo que se pide, nunca antes.
segments: Some background can help, but it should follow the request: last year
only twelve people came, so we moved the event to a weekend.
teaching.audioText: Some background can help, but it should follow the request: last year only twelve people came, so we moved the event to a weekend.

teaching.en: To get to the point, separate what is essential from what is merely a detail: the start time is essential, whereas the parking is not.
teaching.es: Para ir al grano, separa lo esencial de lo que es solo un detalle: la hora de inicio es esencial, mientras que el aparcamiento no lo es.
teaching.explanationEs: Essential es lo que el lector necesita para actuar; un detail es información de apoyo que puede esperar.
segments: To get to the point, separate what is essential from what is merely
a detail: the start time is essential, whereas the parking is not.
teaching.audioText: To get to the point, separate what is essential from what is merely a detail: the start time is essential, whereas the parking is not.

teaching.en: If a message hides its request in the third paragraph, readers may miss it, and then nobody will be able to meet a deadline.
teaching.es: Si un mensaje esconde su petición en el tercer párrafo, los lectores pueden pasarla por alto y entonces nadie podrá cumplir un plazo.
teaching.explanationEs: Request es lo que se pide; si queda escondida, el plazo (meet a deadline) se pierde.
segments: If a message hides its request in the third paragraph, readers may
miss it, and then nobody will be able to meet a deadline.

teaching.en: The bottom line is that we lack one more volunteer, so please confirm your place today and ask a neighbour to do the same.
teaching.es: La conclusión principal es que nos falta un voluntario más, así que confirma hoy tu plaza y pide a un vecino que haga lo mismo.
teaching.explanationEs: The bottom line is that + oración anuncia la conclusión que el lector debe recordar.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje y elige su titular: lo que se necesita ahora.

choices.text: Only nine people came to the garden day last spring.
The committee changed the date after a poor turnout.
We are two drivers short for Saturday.

feedback.es: El titular dice qué se necesita ahora: dos conductores; el dato del año pasado y el cambio de fecha son contexto.

hint.es: El titular dice qué se necesita ahora, no qué pasó antes.

origin.text: Hi all. Last spring only nine people came to the garden day, so the committee changed the date. This year we are two drivers short for Saturday. Could anyone help? Please let me know by Thursday.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Podría alguien cubrir un turno en el banco de alimentos?»

feedback.es: Cover a shift es la colocación natural para ocupar el turno de otra persona; take y work también se usan.

hint.es: Es el verbo que se combina con «a shift» cuando alguien ocupa un turno vacío.

origin.text: We are two people short on Saturday morning. Could anyone ___ a shift at the food bank? I will send the final list on Friday.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con la función que cumple en un mensaje.

pairs.es: da contexto, después de lo esencial

feedback.es: Cada expresión señala qué tipo de información llega: conclusión, contexto, petición o novedad.

hint.es: Piensa en qué pregunta responde cada expresión.

pairs.es: da contexto, después de lo esencial

prompt.es: Escucha la nota y elige qué espera Sara de quienes tienen coche.

choices.text: That they send their names before the weekend.
That they learn the route before Sunday.
That they drive on Friday instead of Sunday.

feedback.es: La petición es responder con nombres antes del viernes; la ruta se explicará después y no es lo que pide ahora.

origin.audio: Hi everyone, it's Sara. I'll keep this short, because I know most of you only listen to the first few seconds. We're two drivers short for the food drive on Sunday, so could anyone with a car reply to me by Friday? I'll explain the route afterwards, but the route isn't the point right now. I just need names by Friday.

prompt.es: Elige el mensaje que pone primero lo esencial y deja el contexto para el final.

choices.text: Last year attendance fell, so the committee met twice and changed the day. As a result, we now need two more volunteers for Saturday's shift; please confirm by Thursday.
We need two more volunteers for Saturday's shift; please confirm by Thursday. Some background: attendance fell last year.
Before I ask anything, let me explain how the event began ten years ago. Later I will tell you what we need.

feedback.es: El primer mensaje abre con lo que se necesita y con el plazo; el segundo contiene lo mismo, pero enterrado tras el contexto.

prompt.es: Completa: «El aparcamiento es un detalle menor, pero la hora de inicio es esencial.»

feedback.es: Detail es la información de apoyo que no cambia lo que el lector debe hacer, frente a lo esencial.

origin.text: I know you are busy, so I will get to the point: the parking is a minor ___, but the start time is essential.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hizo Sara de forma distinta en el mensaje de esta semana.

choices.text: She removed the history of the food drive completely.
She sent the message only to the drivers who had not confirmed.
She moved the request and the deadline to the opening line.

feedback.es: Ahora la primera línea contiene la petición y el plazo; la historia no se elimina, pasa al final como contexto.

origin.audio: At Monday's volunteers' meeting, Sara explained why she had revised the weekly message. Last month, she said, half the group missed the request because it came after three paragraphs of history, and two drivers never confirmed. So this time the first line reads: we need two drivers for Sunday, please confirm by Friday noon. The history of the food drive, the old route and the parking rules come afterwards, as background, for anyone who wants them. She added that nobody would complain if the message were shorter.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender Sara sobre el mensaje del mes pasado?

choices.text: Its request was easy to miss because of the way it was organised.
Its readers were careless and ignored every message she wrote.
Its background was too short to explain the situation properly.

feedback.es: Sara atribuye el fallo a la estructura del mensaje (la petición llegaba tras tres párrafos), no a la falta de atención general ni a un contexto escaso.

origin.audio: At Monday's volunteers' meeting, Sara explained why she had revised the weekly message. Last month, she said, half the group missed the request because it came after three paragraphs of history, and two drivers never confirmed. So this time the first line reads: we need two drivers for Sunday, please confirm by Friday noon. The history of the food drive, the old route and the parking rules come afterwards, as background, for anyone who wants them. She added that nobody would complain if the message were shorter.

prompt.es: Completa: «Muchos lectores solo leen la primera línea, así que empieza por tu petición.»

feedback.es: Lead with + petición es la colocación para abrir un mensaje con lo esencial; start y open también funcionan con with.

origin.text: Most readers read only the first line, so ___ with your request and leave the background until later.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La conclusión principal es que aún faltan dos voluntarios.»

answer.text: The bottom line is that we still need two volunteers

feedback.es: Después de The bottom line is that viene una oración completa con sujeto y verbo: la idea que el lector debe recordar.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje de Leo: ¿qué defecto tiene según lo aprendido en la clase?

choices.text: The writer sounds too blunt when he asks for help.
The request appears only after a long stretch of background.
The deadline is given, but the day of the event is missing.

feedback.es: Leo cuenta primero el contexto del año pasado y deja la petición para el final, así que el plazo se puede pasar por alto; el día del evento sí aparece.

origin.text: Hi team, I hope you had a good weekend. Last time we ran the collection, traffic was terrible and the school gate was closed, which delayed everything by an hour. Anyway, in case it is useful, we could use two more volunteers on Saturday at nine, and it would be great to know by Thursday.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender Tom sobre quien no responda esta noche.

choices.text: They will receive a second reminder at six.
They can still board the coach at half past.
Their place may go to another person.

feedback.es: Si no hay confirmación, Tom dará la plaza a alguien de la lista de espera; la hora del autobús cambió a las ocho.

origin.audio: Right, a quick one from Tom. I'm sorry this is last minute, but the coach leaves at eight, not half past. Could everyone who said yes please confirm again by six tonight? If I don't hear from you, I'll assume you can't come and offer your place to someone on the waiting list.

prompt.es: Completa: «Todo sobre el menú es útil, pero no es esencial para que el lector actúe.»

feedback.es: Essential es lo que el lector necesita para actuar; el resto es detalle y puede esperar al final.

origin.text: Everything about the lunch menu is useful, but it is not ___ for the reader to act, so it can wait until the end.
